skill.name: send-experiment-designer
skill.description: Designs email A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out experiments using user-provided campaign data. Produces hypotheses, variant matrices, sample plans, and evidence-based read-outs without choosing business actions.
skill.summary: Plan rigorous email experiments and read campaign results with clear statistical limits.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and relative documentation links. One documented local Python invocation remains a medium-risk command-execution surface because its data placeholders should be validated before command construction. The skill explicitly treats exports as untrusted data and requires owner-approved decision rules.

remediation.issue: Local statistical command accepts placeholders derived from supplied experiment data.
remediation.suggestion: Validate every event count, sample size, alpha, and minimum-lift value as a bounded numeric argument. Invoke the script through an argument array rather than interpolated shell text.

content.value_statement: Email teams can mistake random variation for a meaningful result. This skill creates test plans and read-outs that separate statistical evidence, practical impact, guardrails, and decision ownership.
actual_capabilities: Select an A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out experiment mode.
Write a falsifiable hypothesis and an isolated variant matrix.
Define primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for an email test.
Plan sample size, minimum detectable effect, power, and run duration.
Read user-provided campaign results using effect size, intervals, and practical thresholds.
Apply an action rule only when a named owner precommitted that rule.
limitations: It relies on baseline rates and result exports supplied by the user.
It does not write email copy or choose a business action independently.
It cannot replace legal, privacy, deliverability, or statistical expert review.
Small lists may not support detecting small effects within a practical duration.

use_cases.title: Plan a subject-line test
use_cases.description: Create a controlled two-cell test with an open-rate target, sample requirement, and guardrails.

use_cases.title: Assess send-time experiments
use_cases.description: Compare randomized send windows while holding audience and creative variables constant.

use_cases.title: Measure incremental email impact
use_cases.description: Design or read a hold-out test using conversion or revenue-per-recipient results.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: subject-line test
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a simple email A/B test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test. My baseline open rate is 38%, my list is 12,000, and I want to detect a 3-point lift.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: send-time test
prompt_templates.scenario: Test a weekly newsletter delivery window.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a send-time experiment for my weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40%, the list is 20,000, and I can send daily.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: multivariate plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess whether a multi-cell design is adequately powered.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a 2 by 2 subject and CTA experiment. Baseline click rate is 2.1%, available audience is 100,000, and the minimum useful lift is 0.5 points.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: hold-out read-out
prompt_templates.scenario: Interpret campaign results without making an unapproved decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this hold-out result: treatment delivered 20,000 with 600 conversions; control delivered 20,000 with 510 conversions. Report effect, uncertainty, guardrails, and decision status.

output_examples.input: Plan a subject-line test with a 38% baseline open rate and a 3-point target lift.
output: Plan: control and one subject-line variant with a fixed read date
Decision status: requires a named owner and precommitted action rule

output_examples.input: Review a completed campaign export with variant delivery and conversion counts.
output: Statistical and practical-effect flags reported separately
Guardrail review for unsubscribes, complaints, and bounces
Decision status remains undecided without an owner-approved rule

best_practices: Change one variable per test cell and keep a control group.
Set the primary metric, sample target, read date, and guardrails before sending.
Use conversion or revenue metrics for hold-out tests instead of open rates alone.
anti_patterns: Do not declare a winner from an early or unplanned result check.
Do not test multiple content changes in one A/B cell.
Do not treat statistical significance as automatic business approval.

faq.question: Which experiment modes are supported?
faq.answer: It supports A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out experiment designs.

faq.question: What data do I need to start?
faq.answer: For a design, provide a baseline rate, audience size, and minimum useful lift. For a read-out, provide per-variant delivery and outcome counts.

faq.question: Can it choose the winning campaign?
faq.answer: No. It reports evidence and can apply only an owner-approved precommitted action rule.

faq.question: Can it test email copy?
faq.answer: It designs the experiment but does not write the subject line, body, or call to action.

faq.question: Why does it use guardrail metrics?
faq.answer: A positive primary metric can still be harmful if unsubscribe, complaint, or bounce rates worsen.

faq.question: What happens when the list is too small?
faq.answer: It recommends a larger detectable effect, a longer run, fewer cells, lower power, or no test.
